title: Basic Directions
source: MindSpark Grade 4 Aptitude & Reasoning | Chapter 4: Basic Directions
subtopics: The four main directions: North, South, East, West
Where are you facing after a turn?
Simple map reading — moving on a grid
learningGoals: Name and point to the four main directions.
Work out which direction you face after turning left or right.
Follow a simple set of direction steps on a grid and find the final position.
coreIdeas: Never Eat Soggy Waffles — North, East, South, West going clockwise.
Opposite of North is South; opposite of East is West.
Turning RIGHT means the next direction clockwise; turning LEFT means going anticlockwise.

workedExamples.problem: Priya is facing North. She turns right. Which direction is she facing now?
workedExamples.solution: Going clockwise from North: North → East. She is now facing East.
workedExamples.concept: Turn right = move one step clockwise

workedExamples.problem: Ravi walks 3 steps East and then 3 steps South. In which direction is he from the starting point?
workedExamples.solution: Going East moves him right; going South moves him down. He is now to the South-East of the starting point.

workedExamples.problem: The sun rises in the East. Tina is watching the sunrise. Which direction is behind her?
workedExamples.solution: If East is in front of Tina, then West is directly behind her — they are opposites.

onboarding.coachIntro: Spark the coach starts Directions by drawing a compass on the board and asking the learner: 'If you stand facing the rising sun, which direction are you facing?' to build intuition. Then Spark teaches the clockwise NESW order and the turning rules before exercises.
onboarding.placementRule: Start at Group A for all learners. If two consecutive wrong answers in Groups A–B, redraw the compass rose and physically demonstrate turns before continuing.

mission.missionPromise: By the end, you will know all four directions, turn left or right without confusion, and read a simple map — like a real explorer!
mission.successCelebration: Award a badge pulse and coach cheer after every correct group. At lesson end, show 'Navigator' trophy.

microLessonPattern: Coach opens with a real-world navigation hook.
Coach draws a compass rose and labels directions.
Coach reads the practice question with a physical turning cue.
Instant feedback refers back to the compass rose.
Review question confirms mastery before next group.

rewardLoop.xpUnit: Award 10 to 20 XP per exercise group.
rewardLoop.streakRule: Show streak counter; protect with one free retry before streak breaks.
rewardLoop.badgeRule: Each group unlocks one badge tied to the direction skill.
rewardLoop.celebrationStyle: Quick coach praise + XP pulse + progress rail tick after every correct answer.

reviewLoop.trigger: Two incorrect attempts triggers a mini-reteach with the compass rose drawn fresh.
reviewLoop.practiceStyle: Offer a simpler question with only two directions involved.
reviewLoop.masteryRule: Advance only after a correct answer with direction named clearly.
reviewLoop.revisitRule: Any group with two errors returns at the next session.

beats.teacherLine: Hey there, explorer! Have you ever wondered how people find their way without Google Maps? They use directions — North, South, East, and West! These four directions are like the four walls of a room for the whole world. Today you will learn to use them perfectly and navigate your way through any map or direction puzzle. Here is a secret memory trick: Never Eat Soggy Waffles — that is North, East, South, West going clockwise!
beats.boardAction: Draw a large compass rose in the centre. Label N at top, E at right, S at bottom, W at left. Write 'NESW clockwise' beside it. Below write: Opposite pairs — N↔S, E↔W.
beats.checkpointPrompt: Quick warm-up: If you face North and turn so your back is to the North, which direction are you facing now?
beats.expectedStudentResponse: South — it is opposite to North.
beats.fallbackHint: North and South are directly opposite. If North is in front, turning your back to it means you now face South.

beats.teacherLine: Watch me do a turning problem! Sam is facing North. He turns right. Where is he facing? I look at the compass — clockwise from North is East. So Sam is facing East. Now he turns right AGAIN — clockwise from East is South. Easy! The rule is: turn right = next direction clockwise. Turn left = go the opposite way (anticlockwise).
beats.boardAction: Draw compass rose. Draw arrow pointing N. Label it 'Sam faces North'. Draw curved clockwise arrow to E. Write '+1 right turn = East'. Draw another curved clockwise arrow to S. Write '+1 more right turn = South'.
beats.checkpointPrompt: Your turn: Meena is facing West. She turns left once. Which direction is she facing?
beats.expectedStudentResponse: South — turning left from West goes anticlockwise: West → South.
beats.fallbackHint: Left turn = anticlockwise. Going anticlockwise from West: W → S. Meena faces South!

beats.teacherLine: Compass in your head — you are ready! Work through Groups A to F. Keep the compass rose in mind for every question. Left = anticlockwise, Right = clockwise. And remember: opposite pairs are N-S and E-W. Go explore!
beats.boardAction: Show cheatsheet: Clockwise order N→E→S→W→N. Anticlockwise order N→W→S→E→N. Opposite pairs: N↔S, E↔W. Sunrise in East, Sunset in West.
beats.checkpointPrompt: Before we start — what are the two opposite direction pairs?
beats.fallbackHint: Look at the compass: N is at top, S at bottom — they are directly opposite. E is on the right, W on the left — opposite too. So N↔S and E↔W.

svgAnimation.text: Clockwise (RIGHT turns): N → E → S → W → N
Anticlockwise (LEFT turns): N → W → S → E → N

sessionFlow.subtopic: The four main directions: North, South, East, West
sessionFlow.missionStepTitle: Exercise A: Name the Four Directions
sessionFlow.coachHook: Let's figure this out together! N, E, S, W — once you know the order, direction questions are easy!

boardDemo.title: Compass Rose — Four Directions
steps: Draw a compass: North at top, East at right, South at bottom, West at left
Memory trick: Never Eat Soggy Waffles (N-E-S-W clockwise)
Opposite pairs: North ↔ South, East ↔ West
boardDemo.teacherLine: Hold your right hand out — that is East! Your left hand is West. Face North (towards East's rising sun side) and South is behind you.

sessionFlow.readAloudPrompt: If North is in front of you and you are facing the board, which direction is on your right?
sessionFlow.tryPrompt: In which direction does the sun set every evening?
sessionFlow.instantFeedbackWin: Correct! The sun sets in the West every evening. East for sunrise, West for sunset — now you will never forget!
sessionFlow.instantFeedbackRetry: Here's a trick: the sun rises in the East and sets in the West. Sunset = West. West is on the left side of the compass.
sessionFlow.reviewPrompt: Quick: what is the direction OPPOSITE to East?

sessionFlow.coachHook: Let's figure this out together! Every direction has an opposite — they face away from each other like two people standing back to back.

boardDemo.title: Opposites on the Compass
steps: North (top) ↔ South (bottom) — exactly opposite
East (right) ↔ West (left) — exactly opposite
If you face North, behind you is South
If you face East, behind you is West
boardDemo.teacherLine: Opposites are always across the compass from each other. Imagine a see-saw — one end goes up while the other goes down. North and South are like that see-saw!

sessionFlow.readAloudPrompt: Ananya is walking towards the North. In which direction is she moving away from?
sessionFlow.tryPrompt: Your turn: Kabir is facing West. What direction is directly behind him?
sessionFlow.instantFeedbackWin: Yes! West and East are opposites. If Kabir faces West, East is directly behind him!
sessionFlow.instantFeedbackRetry: Here's a trick: East ↔ West are opposites, just like North ↔ South. If you face West, you have your back to the East.
sessionFlow.reviewPrompt: Quick: a bird flies North. In what direction is it flying away from its starting point according to the opposite direction?

sessionFlow.missionStepTitle: Exercise C: Left Turns and Right Turns
sessionFlow.coachHook: Let's figure this out together! Left and right turns change which way you face. Use the compass to track every turn!

boardDemo.title: Turning on the Compass
steps: Start: facing North
One right turn (clockwise): facing East
Two right turns: facing South
Three right turns: facing West
Four right turns: back to North (full circle!)
boardDemo.teacherLine: Think of turning right as moving your finger clockwise around the compass — like the hands of a clock. Every right turn moves you one step clockwise: N→E→S→W→N.

sessionFlow.readAloudPrompt: Priya faces North and turns right twice. Which direction is she facing now?
sessionFlow.tryPrompt: Your turn: Rohan faces South and turns left once. Which direction is he facing?
sessionFlow.instantFeedbackWin: Perfect! Left from South = anticlockwise: South → East. Rohan faces East!
sessionFlow.instantFeedbackRetry: Here's a trick: left turn = anticlockwise. From South, going anticlockwise: S → E. So Rohan faces East.
sessionFlow.reviewPrompt: Quick: if you face East and turn right twice, which direction do you face?

sessionFlow.subtopic: Where are you facing after a turn?
sessionFlow.coachHook: Let's figure this out together! Multiple turns can be tricky — count each turn carefully on the compass!

boardDemo.title: Multiple Turns — Count Each One
steps: Start: facing West
Turn right: West → North
Turn right again: North → East
Final direction: East
Shortcut: 2 right turns = move 2 steps clockwise from start
boardDemo.teacherLine: For multiple turns, simply count the steps clockwise (for right) or anticlockwise (for left) from where you started. You can use fingers on the compass to count!

sessionFlow.readAloudPrompt: Sana faces North. She turns left 3 times. What direction does she face after all three turns?
sessionFlow.tryPrompt: Your turn: Dev faces East. He turns right 3 times. Which direction is he facing now?
sessionFlow.instantFeedbackWin: Brilliant! 3 right turns clockwise from East: East→South→West→North. Dev faces North!
sessionFlow.instantFeedbackRetry: Here's a trick: count 3 clockwise steps from East on the compass: E (start), S (turn 1), W (turn 2), N (turn 3). Dev faces North.
sessionFlow.reviewPrompt: Quick: start facing South, turn left twice — which direction now?

sessionFlow.subtopic: Simple map reading — moving on a grid
sessionFlow.missionStepTitle: Exercise E: Moving on a Grid
sessionFlow.coachHook: Let's figure this out together! A grid is like a map. North = up, South = down, East = right, West = left. Follow the steps and find where you land!

boardDemo.title: Grid Movement
steps: Start at a dot in the middle of the grid
Move 2 steps North (up 2 squares)
Move 3 steps East (right 3 squares)
Mark the final position
Final position: 2 up and 3 to the right of start
boardDemo.teacherLine: On a grid, North is always up, South is down, East is right, and West is left. Move step by step — do not try to jump ahead. Mark each position as you go!

sessionFlow.readAloudPrompt: A robot starts at the centre of a grid. It moves 4 steps East. Where is it now relative to the centre?
sessionFlow.tryPrompt: Your turn: a cat starts at position A. It walks 2 steps North, then 2 steps East. Describe its final position.
sessionFlow.masteryCheck: 2 squares above and 2 squares to the right of position A.
sessionFlow.instantFeedbackWin: Exactly! North = up 2, East = right 2. The cat is at the top-right from where it started. Super grid navigation!
sessionFlow.instantFeedbackRetry: Here's a trick: each step in a direction moves you one square that way. North = up. East = right. Move 2 up first, then 2 right. Mark where you end up!
sessionFlow.reviewPrompt: Quick: from start, go 3 steps West and 1 step South. Where is your final position relative to the start?

sessionFlow.missionStepTitle: Exercise F: Sun and Shadow Clues
sessionFlow.coachHook: Let's figure this out together! The sun gives us direction clues every day. Sunrise = East, Sunset = West, Noon sun = South (in India). Shadows always point away from the sun!

boardDemo.title: Sun Clues for Directions
steps: Sunrise is always in the East
Sunset is always in the West
At noon, the sun is in the South (in India)
Shadows point AWAY from the sun
If the sun is in the East (morning), shadows point West
boardDemo.teacherLine: Shadows are like arrows pointing away from the sun. If you know where the sun is, you know where the shadow points — and that tells you East or West!

sessionFlow.readAloudPrompt: In the morning, the sun is in the East. A tree casts a shadow. Which direction does the shadow point?
sessionFlow.tryPrompt: Your turn: at sunset, the sun is in the West. Which direction does a pole's shadow point?
sessionFlow.masteryCheck: East — the shadow points away from the sun (West), so it points East.
sessionFlow.instantFeedbackWin: Correct! Sun in West → shadow points the opposite way → East. You read the sun like a compass!
sessionFlow.instantFeedbackRetry: Here's a trick: shadows always run away from the sun. Sun is in the West = shadow runs towards the East (the opposite direction).
sessionFlow.reviewPrompt: Final: at noon, the sun is roughly in the South. Which direction does your shadow point?
